PASS-WITH-NOTES -- performance/333, ROUND 1, exact head 50c675ac58318d9303a062b890ec649d47806cea.

The executable delta is one pre-send predicate in detach_pane_taps: a listed, owned pane already clear (no pipe and no marker) takes the existing release_tap path instead of entering pending. It reuses the INITIAL tap_states snapshot; no additional read, timer, loop, kernel launch or spawn site is added. Ownership selection remains unchanged. This is a BRAKE on issuing tmux commands: removing it sends the same panes or more. The existing local map removal/sink unlink now happens before command construction; it is not cost-free, but adds no new kind of side effect.

Launch bound unchanged: let P be the initial input and A the owned, still-attached entries admitted to pending. Healthy writes are greedy 8KiB byte-packed chunks of A, not a universal ceil(P/130); with uniform widths C panes/chunk, ceil(A/C). Approximately130 assumes typical pane-ID widths;145 attached taps still need2. A clear-only set needs the initial read and existing release/unlink work, but0 batch writes.

Every continuing batch round still removes pending entries, so aggregate counted batch writes B<=A<=P; successful chunks are not resent. This is NOT an all-process stop bound or a per-target-attempt guarantee under mixed vanish/failure. Scoped reads remain normally1+B+convergence rereads; existing control startup/fallback reads can launch. Snapshot/vector/ownership/unlink work remains. The2s remains convergence grace, not child/stop wall-time ceiling. The docs correctly qualify these costs. No steady-state per-seat work is introduced: this path runs on stop or explicit tap retirement.
